learning_outcomes.text: The student can describe the major principles of object-oriented programming.
The student can apply the different principles in an assignment.
The student analyzes the problem and translates it into a program structure and associated algorithms.
The student converts the structure into a program using C++ code.
The student converts the algorithms into the program using C++ code.
The student verifies the operation of the program against the requirements of the assignment.

assessment_rules: The course is evaluated based on two activities: a theory exam and a lab exam. Each activity evaluates separate learning objectives. The theory exam evaluates learning objectives (1) - (3), and the lab exam evaluates learning objectives (3) - (6). If the student achieves a score of less than 7 on one of the evaluation activities, the student can achieve a maximum of 9/20 for the entire course unit. For resits, successful partial results for "Object Oriented Programming: Theory" and "Object Oriented Programming: Lab" can be carried over within the academic year.
